interface.title: Cell Surveillance — single-cell tracking v0.4.0 (Streamlit)
interface.field: Cell biology / live-cell fluorescence microscopy (nuclear envelope rupture, cell migration, cell fate)
interface.stage_of_work: Image analysis of time-lapse movies, from calibration and tracking through quantification, review and export
interface.what_it_is_for: Load a fluorescent-reporter time-lapse movie, calibrate time and scale, track every nucleus, then review and export per-cell measurements of nuclear ruptures, movement, divisions and deaths, for the whole field or a cropped region.

data.note: Server-side synthetic movie /work/app/examples/demo_movie.tif, typed into the 'or paste a path' box (60 frames, 320×320 px, no scale bar). Calibrated at 5 min/frame and 0.3 µm/px, later recalibrated to 10 min/frame and 0.6 µm/px. The Setup card showed the frame count as '-9223372036854775808 frames', and the Setup Preview crashed with StreamlitInvalidMinMaxError at app.py line 712 (frame slider min == max). Analysis still ran correctly ('60 frames', finished in 8 s). Results: 7 tracks (6 original cells plus daughter 7). Compared with the known ground truth (relabelled: tool cell 2 = GT cell 0, tool 3 = GT 1, tool 6 = GT 2, tool 5 = GT 3): at threshold 0.05 the rupture table matched GT frames exactly (12–16, 35–37, 25–30). At the default threshold 0.1, GT cell 1's rupture was missed. The death was called correctly (cell 5, 205 min, high confidence). The UI rendered in the Light look by default; the Look control was never touched. FINDINGS (tool output contradicts itself or its README): (1) The division's nuclear envelope breakdown (cell 6, frames 28–30) is called a rupture, and the death is called a 'terminal' rupture; the reviewer reports that the README says division breakdown is excluded. (2) The Divisions table lists one division (frame 36, low confidence, daughter_b = 7, daughter_a = None), but the Overview Divisions card and the 'How each track ended' chart both show 0 divisions (screens/040.webp). (3) After Apply at threshold 0.05, the History card still reads 4 ruptures (screens/071.webp), so the threshold change does not reach every summary. (4) The replay saw the threshold sweep show 5 ruptures at the 0.1 in use while the KPI card said 4. REPLAY CAVEATS: the replay loaded a different path (sample_data/demo_movie.tif) at 0.325 µm/px, and its screenshots are under check/screens/, so its screen numbers do not refer to this run's screens. Its 'not_confirmed' marks on t6 and t11–t14 come from running out of action budget, not from contradicting evidence. The replay also reported two behaviours this run did not see: dragging a Region box left the Left/Right/Top/Bottom fields unchanged, and ticking a cell in the Cells table did not redraw the reporter trace.

features.name: Stepped setup wizard with readiness checklist
features.general: Enter the input, its calibration and the analysis options in numbered cards; a checklist shows what is still missing and the run button stays disabled until everything is set
features.specific: Movie → Calibrate (minutes/frame, scale bar / pixel size / no scale) → Measure (6 checkboxes) → Run, with the ✓/○ checklist and the 'Still needed: …' hint
steps: Give a file path (or drop/browse a file)
Enter the frame interval
Pick a scale mode and value
Tick measurements and outputs
Press Analyse movie once the checklist is all ✓ and watch the staged progress log
serves_tasks: Calibrate the time between images and the spatial scale

features.name: Event-threshold tuner with sensitivity sweep
features.general: Choose the signal that defines an event and a threshold, see how many events each threshold would call, and apply it so the event tables and plots update
features.specific: Ruptures tab: Measure dropdown (ratio rise, cytoplasm rise, ratio, intensity) + Threshold slider + Apply, with the 'Ruptures called at each threshold' curve marking the value 'in use', and duration/size/per-cell histograms that refresh. Setup has the same choice as an auto/manual popover. In this run the History card still showed the pre-Apply rupture count.
steps: Pick the event metric
Read the threshold sweep curve to find a plateau
Drag the threshold slider
Press Apply and wait for re-calling
Check the 'in use' marker and the updated histograms and counts
serves_tasks: Detect transient events and tune the detection threshold
Choose which measurements and outputs to compute, and how events are defined

features.name: Event gallery: image strips with aligned signal traces
features.general: Review detected events one by one as a short filmstrip of the object around the event, next to its signal trace with the event span shaded, ordered by size, duration or time
features.specific: Look at individual ruptures: Show = Largest / Smallest / Longest / In order; each row shows 'Cell N · starts t · lasts m · size s', a 10-frame strip with ruptured frames underlined in red, and a ratio trace with a blue band
steps: Pick an ordering (Largest/Smallest/Longest/In order)

Compare the shaded span on the trace with the strip frames
Open a strip fullscreen if needed
